holding_summary: Boundary/ejectment dispute over a strip of land between a factory lot and adjoining dwelling lots, decided on the rule that monuments on the ground control courses and distances in a sheriff's deed.
notes: Retrieved only because 'Lodge' is a party surname; case concerns land-survey boundary law, not letting of rooms or lodgers.

cite: Cumberland Valley Railroad v. McLanahan, 59 Pa. 23
holding_summary: Ejectment by a tenant in common against a railroad company that built a warehouse beyond its chartered right of way on land held partly under a license from a co-tenant.
notes: Concerns railroad corporate powers and a license to occupy land for a warehouse, not household letting of dwelling rooms; retrieval matched generic ejectment/tenant language.

holding_summary: Ejectment involving competing paper titles, adverse possession, and the doctrine that a trustee holding legal title may sue all but the equitable owner.
notes: City-lot boundary and title dispute; no occupancy-for-pay or lodging issue present.

holding_summary: Holds that equity cannot enjoin a landlord's statutory Landlord and Tenant Act proceeding to recover possession, even though the underlying dispute involved a bank's lease of two rooms in a hotel building for banking purposes.
notes: Underlying facts involve a commercial lease of hotel rooms to a bank, but the opinion addresses only equity jurisdiction versus the statutory landlord-tenant remedy; no discussion of letting/lodging character or duration.

holding_summary: Dispute over a coal-mining lease's grant of use of tenements/railroad fixtures for extracting coal, holding that use for removing other coal was unauthorized and that assumpsit (rather than case) was the wrong form of action.
notes: 'Tenements' here means mining structures/cabins incident to a coal lease, not dwelling rooms let to lodgers.

holding_summary: In a suit on a marital separation agreement, holds that evidence of a parol side-agreement letting the wife occupy the husband's house rent-free until a date certain, and her failure to vacate, was admissible as a set-off.
notes: Wife's continued occupancy of husband's house after separation is a domestic-relations/support matter, not compensated letting of rooms to a lodger or boarder.

holding_summary: Holds a husband not liable, merely by virtue of his duty to support his wife, for rent on a house his wife had leased before their marriage and continued to occupy after it, while he himself resided elsewhere at a boarding-house.
notes: Husband's residence at 'his boarding-house' is a passing background fact; the holding concerns spousal liability for a pre-marital lease debt, not the legal character of lodging/boarding arrangements.

cite: Lanigan ex rel. Stichter v. Kille, 97 Pa. 120
holding_summary: Sets the measure of damages for a lessee evicted by paramount title from an ore-mining lease as the consideration paid, denying recovery for the value of mining improvements erected under covenant.
notes: Commercial mining lease and covenant-for-title damages case; unrelated to household lodging or boarding.

holding_summary: Holds that a landlord may appeal from a justice of the peace's decision allowing a tenant's set-off against rent under the Act of 1810, even though the tenant himself has no right of appeal.
notes: Ordinary dwelling-house tenancy rent/set-off appeal procedure; no lodging-house licensing or short-term letting issue.

holding_summary: In a summary proceeding for possession for non-payment of rent, holds the tenant may defend by showing the landlord's title has since been divested by a sheriff's sale under a judgment that encumbered it before the lease began.
notes: Ordinary rent-recovery/title-divestment dispute; not about lodging houses or short-term room letting.

cite: Reed v. Fidelity Insurance Trust & Safe Deposit Co., 113 Pa. 574
holding_summary: Holds that in partition among tenants in common, a mortgage lien on one co-tenant's undivided interest shifts from the land to the owelty payable to that co-tenant.
notes: Partition/lien-priority dispute among trust beneficiaries and tenants in common; unrelated to lodging or letting of dwellings.

holding_summary: Holds a railroad company could remove machinery and fixtures from a shop built on land granted subject to a reverter clause, up until actual abandonment of the site.
notes: Railroad land-grant reverter and fixture-removal dispute; no lodging or dwelling-letting issue.

holding_summary: In distributing sheriff's-sale proceeds, holds that goods of a sub-tenant of a storeroom remain liable for the principal landlord's unpaid rent even though the sub-tenant had paid his own rent in full to the immediate lessee.
notes: Commercial storeroom sub-letting and distress-for-rent priority dispute; not household lodging.

holding_summary: Replevin case holding that an avowry for distress of rent in arrear need not state the exact amount due, and a landlord may recover less than the sum avowed.
notes: Lease of a store and barn; pure pleading/distress-for-rent technicality, unrelated to lodging.

holding_summary: Holds that an owner may not remove his half of a long-standing division fence built jointly with an adjoining landowner without consent, as the fence has become part of the realty.
notes: Boundary-fence dispute between adjoining owners; unrelated to lodging or letting.

holding_summary: Trespass action over a sawmill operator's refusal to divide manufactured lumber with the landowner under a wood-cutting agreement; holds an agent with no title until division cannot lawfully retain and remove the whole.
notes: Sawmill/timber-division contract dispute; unrelated to lodging or dwelling letting.

holding_summary: Adopts the 'American doctrine' that no easement of light and air over an adjoining lot is implied from conveyance of a house with windows overlooking it, absent real necessity.
notes: Light-and-air easement dispute between adjoining lot owners; unrelated to lodging.

holding_summary: Holds an outgoing farm tenant may sell his right to the way-going crop, and the purchaser's claim survives a later settlement between landlord and tenant cancelling the lease.
notes: Agricultural farm-lease way-going-crop dispute; unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.
